title: Shawarma Bar Night
shortDescription: Spiced chicken shawarma with flatbread and fixings for ten
subtitle: Spiced chicken shawarma with flatbread and fixings for ten
description: Marinated chicken thighs roast on sheet pans with shawarma spices, then slice thin for a build bar with flatbread, tahini, pickles, tomatoes, and onions. Each crew member assembles their own wrap at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Shawarma Bar Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.instruction: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, paprika, turmeric, garlic, and 2 tbsp salt. Coat thighs and marinate at least 2 hours or overnight for deepest flavor penetration.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Arrange thighs on oiled sheet pans skin-side up. Roast at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until charred at edges and internal temp reaches 175°F in the thickest piece. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Rest and slice thin
steps.instruction: Rest chicken 10 minutes, then slice as thin as possible against the grain. Pile into a hotel pan and tent with foil for holding at the bar.

steps.title: Set the shawarma bar
steps.instruction: Warm flatbread wrapped in towels. Arrange sliced chicken, tahini, pickles, diced tomatoes, sliced onions, and fresh parsley in separate labeled pans along the line.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Shawarma Bar Night onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Service and replenish
steps.instruction: Call the meal and demonstrate one wrap build. Replenish chicken and bread from backup pans kept warm in a low oven throughout the meal.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Shawarma Bar Night — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: A pinch of cinnamon in the marinade adds authentic shawarma depth without tasting sweet.
Double-stack sheet pans if thighs release a lot of fat—crisp bottoms need airflow.
Offer hot sauce and garlic sauce in squeeze bottles to keep the line moving fast.
tonightSpread: Full shawarma bar with chicken, flatbread, tahini, pickles, and herb salad.
Cucumber yogurt dip and hummus for crews building bowls instead of wraps.
leftovers: Chop chicken into a grain bowl with leftover bar toppings and lemon dressing.
Stuff into pita with feta for a cold lunch wrap the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shawarma bar night feels like takeout but costs a fraction and scales cleanly. Warm spiced chicken smells incredible in the hall and the DIY format means no one gets stuck with toppings they hate.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate chicken up to 24 hours. Prep all bar toppings in labeled hotel pans the night before. Slice chicken just before service and hold at 165°F in a covered pan with a splash of lemon juice.
